title: Terraform Rules
summary: Project rules for Terraform: module layout, naming, remote state with locking, typed variables, tagging and a reviewed plan before every apply.
description: Infrastructure code changes real systems, so sloppy conventions cost more than they do in an application. These rules give an agent a structure for modules, state and variables that keeps changes small and reviewable.
They also make plans the unit of review: nothing is applied until someone has read exactly what will change.
useWhen: You are adding resources or modules to a Terraform codebase
State is stored on a laptop or shared without locking
Variables have no types or descriptions
Teams apply changes without reading the plan
body:
# Project rules: Terraform

## Layout
- Keep a root configuration per environment (`envs/dev`, `envs/prod`) that calls reusable modules in `modules/`. Each module has `main.tf`, `variables.tf`, `outputs.tf` and `versions.tf`, with a short README.
- Pin the Terraform version and every provider with `required_version` and `required_providers`, and commit `.terraform.lock.hcl`.

## State
- Use a remote backend with locking and encryption, and separate state per environment. Never commit state files or secrets. Do not edit state by hand; use `moved` blocks, `import` blocks or `terraform state` commands with review.

## Style
- Use snake_case resource names, with `this` for a module's single main resource. Give every variable a `type` and `description`, add `validation` blocks where limits exist, and mark sensitive values.
- Prefer `for_each` over `count` so removing an item does not shift others. Avoid over-nested modules and huge `locals`.
- Apply consistent tags through provider `default_tags`, including owner and environment.

## Safety
- Set `prevent_destroy` on stateful resources and use `lifecycle` rules sparingly. Pass secrets from a secret manager, not variables files.

## Before finishing
- Run `terraform fmt -check -recursive`, `terraform validate`, `tflint` and a scanner such as Checkov or Trivy. Run `terraform plan -out=tfplan` and summarize the adds, changes and destroys. Never run `apply` without approval.

example.prompt: Add an S3 bucket for logs with a 90 day lifecycle rule
example.result: The agent adds a module call with typed variables, encryption and public access blocks enabled, default tags applied, then runs fmt, validate, tflint and a plan, and reports one resource to add.

faq.question: Why should the agent not apply on its own?
faq.answer: An apply changes live infrastructure. A person should read the plan first, so the agent stops at the plan and reports it.

faq.question: Does it work with OpenTofu?
faq.answer: Yes. The structure and review rules are the same; use the tofu command in place of terraform.

access: Instructions only; it does not read or run anything by itself
